newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran suspends imports from New Zealand.
newsitem.headline: Iran suspends imports from New Zealand.

text.p: Iran said on Saturday it has suspended imports from New Zealand after Wellington recalled its envoy following a German court ruling that Tehran ordered the 1992 murders of Kurdish activists in Berlin.
The official IRNA news agency said: "Construction Jihad minister Gholamreza Forouzesh said that Iran had suspended New Zealand pending agreements for purchasing meat, butter, and wool."
It quoted Forouzesh as saying that Tehran's action was in response to New Zealand's recalling its ambassador from Tehran and added that Iran was looking for alternative suppliers.
It gave no further details of the agreements.
New Zealand on Friday joined other Western countries who recalled their envoys in reaction to the German court verdict.

The ruling said that the assassinations were ordered by a secret special operations committee whose members included Iran's president, its religious leader, intelligence minister and the head of foreign policy.

But it stopped short of explicitly naming Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani and spiritual leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who prosecutors had accused of ultimate responsibility for the attack in Berlin's Mykonos restaurant.
Iran has repeatedly denied all involvement in the killings which it blames on infighting among opposition groups.
European Union (EU) members, with the exception of Greece, recalled their envoys for consultations following Thursday's verdict, as did Australia.
